chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Buster Harding and the Golden Gate Ballroom with Andy Kirk
summary: Buster Harding arranged and played piano while Wilson fronted; they were house band at the Golden Gate with Andy Kirk, whose band Wilson describes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And then, my right arm in that band was another piano player -- Buster Harding. Buster Harding was my main man for arranging, and a lot of times he'd play piano in the band and I'd stand up in front, because the agents figured that in those days they always would have a front man in the band, and even Chick Webb -- Chick Webb Bardu Ali would play the theatres, he would hire to stand in front of the band with a stick so the agents felt that unless I was being featured on the piano and was playing in the rhythm section, I would stand in front, and then Buster would take over on the piano, so whenever we could, we would actually have two piano instruments on the job, and our main job, which lasted so long, the Golden Gate Ballroom in Harlem, we did have the two pianos there.
What's the name of that ballroom?
And how far was that from the Savoy?

One block down. It was in the old Cotton Club building. The Golden Gate Ballroom. Sometimes on a weekend, there would be five bands in there. But my big band, and Andy Kirk -- we were the house bands, and Andy Kirk had a wonderful band there, too. He had Mary Lou Williams on piano, and Don Byas was his featured tenor. He had

two good tenor players, Don Bias and Dick Wilson -- and he had one of my favorite lead trumpet players, Big Jim -- and I don't know Big Jim's last name, but he was one of the great trumpet players of all time.

Yeah. Jim ... I know his name because he works for the subway now, if he hasn't passed away, because my wife was a friend of his wife's. And they also had a John Williams, MaryLou Williams' husband, who was a baritone sax player.
That's right, John Williams was in that Andy Kirk band, and Floyd Smith was on the guitar.
Oh, a great guitarist. Thigpen on drums, Ed Thigpen's father.
And Ben on drums. Oh, Andy Kirk had a great band. I can't think of his trombone player's name, I think it was Russell Bowells, but Russell Bowells was with Jimmy Lunceford.
He was with Lunceford's band, yes he was.

But any way, Andy Kirk and me, we were the house bands at the Golden Gate, and on weekends, they would augment it; beside us, they would bring in sometimes two other bands, sometimes as many as three more bands.
